newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends slightly higher, topside heavy.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends slightly higher, topside heavy.

text.p: The key March three-month futures contract settled higher on Friday, buoyed by gains in Japanese government bonds (JGBs) and continuing positive sentiment in the wake of a weak Bank of Japan (BOJ) economic outlook released on Thursday, market sources said.
The topside was heavy, however, on pre-weekend book-squaring and profit-taking, keeping March Euroyen stuck in a narrow 99.11-99.13 range. It settled at 99.12.
"The market remains fundamentally strong after the BOJ report, but sales at 99.12 and 99.13 as operators squared their books ahead of the weekend limited gains today," one city bank trader said.

The BOJ said in its report that, while Japan's economy is continuing on a moderate recovery trend, the recovery was unlikely to gather significant momentum in view of fragility in some sectors and continued pressure from balance-sheet adjustments. This confirmed market suspicions that a rate rise later this year was increasingly unlikely, traders said.

With the overall interest rate picture still unclear and some sentiment remaining in the market that a rate rise in December is still possible, operators were hesitant about buying March Euroyen aggressively, the city bank trader said.

The key September JGB futures contract briefly touched a three-month high of 126.02, but then fell back slightly on hedge sales and a large-lot sell order, although the overall tone remained positive.
Traders said that, while Euroyen futures were buoyed by the JGBs' strength, the September JGB contract's failure to extend its gains kept afternoon Euroyen trade lacklustre.

The next key point for March is 99.14, with a break above that likely to lead to quick gains on technical factors, traders said. "The ultimate extent of this rise is hard to predict, but it could make it up to 99.20, particularly if JGB futures rise to around 126.50," the city bank trader said.
He added that the market will be waiting for June industrial production figures, due on July 30, with poor figures likely to send both JGBs and Euroyen futures higher.
The BOJ injected 200 billion yen into the money market this morning, keeping the market in surplus by 300 billion yen for the third consecutive day.
